question.:question/problem: Calculate $2\left(\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡4x}{\sin ^{2}⁡4x}\,\text{d}x\right).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We can write the integral as

$$
2\left(\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡4x}{\sin ^{2}⁡4x}\,\text{d}x\right)=2\left(\int \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡4x}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡4x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡4x}\,\text{d}x\right)
$$

We then use the fact that $\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡4x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡4x}=\operatorname{cot}⁡4x$ and $\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡4x}=\operatorname{csc}⁡4x$ to express this as

$$
2\left(\int \operatorname{csc}⁡4x\operatorname{cot}⁡4x\,\text{d}x\right)
$$

We can solve this by substitution. Let $u=4x.$ Then $\text{d}x=\frac{1}{4}\text{d}u.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}2\left(\int \operatorname{csc}⁡4x\operatorname{cot}⁡4x\,\text{d}x\right)& =2\left(\int \operatorname{csc}⁡u\operatorname{cot}⁡u\,\cdot \frac{1}{4}\text{d}u\right)\\  & =2\left(\frac{1}{4}\int \operatorname{csc}⁡u\operatorname{cot}⁡u\,\text{d}u\right)\\  & =2\left(-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{csc}⁡u\right)+C\\  & =2\left(-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{csc}⁡4x\right)+C\end{aligned}

$$

$$

We then use the fact that $\frac{1}{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}=\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}$ to express this as

$$
\begin{aligned}-1\left(\int \operatorname{cot}⁡x(\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{csc}⁡x)\text{d}x\right)& =-1\left(\int (\operatorname{cot}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cot}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡x)\text{d}x\right)\\  & =-1\left(\int (\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cot}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{csc}⁡x)\text{d}x\right)\\  & =-1\left(\int (\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{cot}⁡x)\text{d}x\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}-1\left(\int \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{csc}⁡x}{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}\,\text{d}x\right)& =-1\left(\int (\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{cot}⁡x)\text{d}x\right)\\  & =-1\left(\operatorname{sin}⁡x-(-\operatorname{csc}⁡x)\right)+C\\  & =-1\left(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{csc}⁡x\right)+C\end{aligned}
